---
params:
  update_data: true
  fn: "life-gotten-expensive-nytimes.csv"
---

## Setup

```{r}
library(readr)
library(googledrive)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
```

## Download

```{r, eval=params$update_data}
#| label: gather-data-from-google
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
if (!dir.exists('../include/csv')) {
  message("Creating missing `csv/`.")
  dir.create("../include/csv")
}

if (params$update_data) {
  options(gargle_oauth_email = Sys.getenv("GMAIL_SURVEY"))
  googledrive::drive_auth()

  googledrive::drive_download(
    "life-gotten-expensive-nytimes",
    path = file.path("../include/csv", params$fn),
    type = "csv",
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
  message("Data updated.")
} else {
  message("Using stored data.")
}
```

## Import

```{r}
#| label: import-data
#| output-location: slide
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
expensive_df <- readr::read_csv(file.path("../include/csv", 
                params$fn), show_col_types = FALSE)

str(expensive_df)
```

## Visualization: Housing

```{r}
#| label: fig-housing
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
#| code-fold: false
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|2|4-5|6-8|9-12"
p_housing <- expensive_df |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "housing") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = year, y = price, color = location, 
      fill = location, shape = price_type) |>
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = price, 
                group = location, color = location)) +
  ylim(0, 1700000) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Price changes in illustrative expenses: mid 1980s-present",
       subtitle = "Housing", 
       caption = "Source: Tavernise et al. (2026).") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 500000, 1000000, 1500000),
    labels = c("0", "500,000", "1,000,000", "1,500,000")
  ) +
  ylab("price ($)") +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 14))

p_housing
```

## Visualization: Childcare

```{r}
#| label: fig-child-care
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
#| code-fold: false
#| 
p_child <- expensive_df |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "child_care") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = year, y = price, color = location, 
      fill = location, shape = price_type) |>
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = price, 
                group = location, color = location)) +
  ylim(0, 450) +
  theme_classic() +   
  labs(title = "Price changes in illustrative expenses: mid 1980s-present",
       subtitle = "Childcare",
       caption = "Source: Tavernise et al. (2026).") +
  ylab("price ($)") +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 14))

p_child
```

## Visualization: Entertainment

```{r}
#| label: fig-entertainment
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Price changes for a set of entertainment expenses. The huge increase in the cost of a Super Bowl ticket is apparent. Price changes in items less than $1,000 are hard to see on this scale."
citation <- "Source: Tavernise et al. (2026)."

p_ent <- expensive_df |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "entertainment") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = year,
      y = price,
      color = category_type,
      fill = category_type) |>
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(
    x = year,
    y = price,
    group = category_type,
    color = category_type
  )) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Price changes in illustrative expenses: mid 1980s-present",
       subtitle = "Entertainment",
       caption = citation) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000, 3000),
    labels = c("0", "1,000", "2,000", "3,000")
  ) +
  ylab("price ($)") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())

p_ent
```

## A composite

```{r}
( p_housing | p_child | p_ent )
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reduce adornments

To make the composite work, I need to reduce some of the plot-specific adornments.

:::

p_ent_2 <- expensive_df |>

  ggplot() +
  aes(x = year,
      y = price,
      color = category_type,
      fill = category_type) |>

    x = year,

(p_housing_2 + plot_spacer() + p_child_2) / (plot_spacer()  + p_ent_2 + plot_spacer())
